allowlist.reason: Guild configuration attribution is retained with the active board settings; member activity erasure removes starrers, not guild policy or its operator attribution.

Configuration attribution is retained with active guild safety/permission settings; member erasure must not delete or broaden policy configuration. A separate reviewed configuration change is required.

May contain configured staff/test actor ID lists. These are control-plane policy, not member activity; removing an entry could weaken or broaden a safety gate. Requires a separate reviewed policy edit.
Immutable configuration audit: the database rejects DELETE/UPDATE/TRUNCATE. Retain operator attribution; no trigger disabling or bypass is authorized by member erasure.
Immutable prior configuration (including policy actor lists); retained for safety change accountability. Not covered by guild-local activity erasure.
Immutable changed configuration (including policy actor lists); retained for safety change accountability. Not covered by guild-local activity erasure.
Global incident-control singleton has no guild scope. Preserve the halt and responder attribution; guild-local erasure must never disengage or rewrite a safety control.
Minimal operator accountability for erasures: actor and time only, never the erased subject, guild, request or content. Actor records are retained independently of member activity.

An operator-released request must retain its caller-supplied key as a replay fence, even if it is a member snowflake; removing or changing this indefinite identity-bearing exception could let delayed delivery repeat the uncertain Discord mutation.
An operator-released request replaces its obsolete ownership token with the fixed non-identity operator_released marker; no live claim can be resumed.
An operator-released request replaces its actor-derived request hash with the fixed non-identity operator_released marker, redacted from inspection/audit snapshots.

Guild-scoped opt-out suppression tombstone: deleting it would silently resume per-user persistence the member refused. Retained until the member opts back in; member erasure never removes suppression.

Opt-out purge receipt scope: one row per purge with operator actor and database timestamp. Retained accountability in the same class as member_erasure_audit; the subject appears only in the scope columns, never in the actor label.
Operator accountability for opt-out purges: actor and time only, never subject content. Retained independently of member activity, like member_erasure_audit.actor.

Replacement-ticket reference on self-role acknowledgement tickets: holds the opaque gen_random_uuid exchange_id of the superseding ticket, never a member identity, so there is no member PII to erase. The value is deleted with its ticket row by the self_role_exchanges plan predicate.

Operator attribution for admin API token issuance: names the issuing operator, never a guild member. Retained like member_erasure_audit.actor; guild-local member erasure must never rewrite credential issuance accountability.

Named human or AI credential principal, potentially identifying a member, retained as credential authority independently of guild activity. Guild-local member erasure must not rewrite holders or silently alter cross-guild grants; revocation and credential retention require a separate authorized operator action. No holder is inferred from an erased subject.
